Despite using the hyperparameter combination that triggers collapse in all 10 tested multi-joint locomotion seeds (Walker/Cheetah), the single-joint Cartpole shows no CIVO, confirming the phenomenon requires multi-joint dynamics where temporal abstraction amplifies the reward fidelity gap.\n135\t\n136\t\\section{NVE Threshold Sensitivity Analysis}\n137\t\\label{sec:appendix_sensitivity}\n138\t\n139\tWe report the full sensitivity analysis for the NVE diagnostic framework introduced in Section~\\ref{sec:results}. The main text reports Task~B2 (any CIVO detection, $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$). Here we additionally present Task~B1, which restricts the positive class to \\emph{sustained} CIVO, specifically experiments exhibiting persistent, accelerating value overestimation that progresses to performance collapse. Transient CIVO cases (e.g., exp~009b, which self-corrects after a brief excursion above the threshold) are classified as negative in B1.\n140\t\n141\t\\subsection{Per-Experiment NVE Values}\n142\t\n143\tTable~\\ref{tab:nve_raw} lists the NVE values at 35K+ training steps for all eleven factorial experiments (including four 008e\\_v3 seeds and exp\\_059). Raising the threshold to $1.7\\times$ loses 009b, dropping recall to 80.0\\%.\n243\t\\item \\textbf{Best F1.} At $1.5\\times$, F1 = 90.9\\%, the highest among all tested thresholds for B2. The single false positive (008e\\_v3\\_s2) is mechanistically identifiable as IRD rather than CIVO.\n244\t\\item \\textbf{Sensitivity--specificity tradeoff.} Lower thresholds ($1.0\\times$) add false positives without gaining true positives. Higher thresholds ($\\geq 1.7\\times$) sacrifice recall without eliminating the 008e\\_v3\\_s2 false positive (which requires $\\tau > 3.78$).\n245\t\\end{enumerate}\n246\t\n247\tFor Task~B1 (sustained CIVO only), the optimal threshold $\\nve \\geq 3.9\\times$ achieves $10/11$ accuracy ($90.9\\%$, 95\\% CI: [58.7\\%, 99.8\\%]); the sole false positive is exp\\_059 (NVE${=}4.72\\times$, self-correcting CIVO classified as B1-negative).\n248\t\n249\t\\subsection{Expanded ROC Analysis}\n250\t\\label{sec:roc_analysis}\n251\t\n252\tThe original $n{=}17$ analysis (Tables~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b1}--\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full}) predates the SGS, RAVE, and TCN experiments. We extend the NVE diagnostic evaluation to $n{=}56$ configurations spanning all tested interventions. Figure~\\ref{fig:nve_roc} shows the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95\\% bootstrap confidence interval (10{,}000 resamples).\n253\t\n254\t\\begin{figure}[h]\n255\t\\centering\n256\t\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_roc_curve.pdf}\n257\t\\caption{NVE ROC curve ($n{=}56$ configurations, AUROC${=}0.990$, comprehensive validation). The preset $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$ operating point (star) achieves TPR${=}1.00$, FPR${=}0.09$, accuracy${=}53/56$, F1${=}0.941$. Three false positives arise from non-CIVO value overestimation: mitigation transient VE spike (008e\\_v3 subsample, $1.93\\times$) and frozen embedding transients (047, $1.71\\times$; 057, $1.88\\times$). Threshold calibrated and validated post-hoc; cross-architecture validation deferred.}\n258\t\\label{fig:nve_roc}\n259\t\\end{figure}\n260\t\n261\t\\begin{figure}[h]\n262\t\\centering\n263\t\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_threshold_prf.pdf}\n264\t\\caption{Precision, Recall, and F1 as a function of NVE threshold ($n{=}56$ configurations). Peak F1${=}0.941$ at $\\tau{=}1.5\\times$, where recall remains perfect ($1.00$) and precision${=}0.889$. The plateau of high F1 across $\\tau \\in [1.5, 1.7]$ indicates robustness to threshold selection.}\n265\t\\label{fig:nve_prf}\n266\t\\end{figure}\n267\t\n268\tWe label a configuration as CIVO-positive if and only if (i)~it uses a trained $\\dt$-embedding with multi-rate data exposure, and (ii)~NVE exceeds $1.5\\times$ with co-occurring entropy collapse. Configurations exhibiting high NVE through other mechanisms (gradient truncation side effects, value anchor pollution) are labeled non-CIVO.\n269\t\n270\tThe three false positives (FPR${=}0.18$) are mechanistically distinct from CIVO: (1)~RAVE anchor pollution (exp\\_028, the EMA anchor becomes inflated, producing overestimation through a different pathway); (2)~obs-decoder SGS-induced value distortion (exp\\_025 seed~2, blocking observation decoder gradients damages the RSSM latent space); (3)~IRD eval-driven collapse (exp\\_008e\\_v3 seed~2, actor entropy \\emph{increases} with evaluation collapse, mechanistically distinct from CIVO's entropy \\emph{decrease}). All three produce NVE $> 1.5\\times$ through non-CIVO mechanisms, indicating that the NVE diagnostic detects value overestimation broadly rather than CIVO specifically---a feature rather than a limitation for practitioners monitoring deployment health. The closest sub-threshold case (008f seed~4, NVE${=}1.41\\times$) lacks $\\dt$-conditioning entirely ($d{=}0$); its elevated NVE reflects transient value noise that self-corrects without the positive feedback loop characteristic of CIVO. The closest above-threshold positive (008d seed~3, NVE${=}1.53\\times$) exhibits the full CIVO causal chain: trained $\\dt$-embedding, entropy decrease, and evaluation collapse to 14\\% of baseline.\n271\t\n272\t\\paragraph{Comprehensive validation ($n{=}56$).}\n273\tExpanding the evaluation set to all classifiable experiments yields $n{=}56$ ($n_{\\text{pos}}{=}24$, $n_{\\text{neg}}{=}32$), spanning Walker Walk, Cheetah Run, and multiple intervention configurations (SGS, TCN, dual-critic, frozen embedding). At the $1.5\\times$ threshold: AUROC${=}0.990$, precision${=}0.889$, recall${=}1.000$, F1${=}0.941$, accuracy${=}53/56$. The three false positives are: exp\\_008e\\_v3\\_subsample ($1.93\\times$, mitigation config with transient VE spike), exp\\_047 ($1.71\\times$, frozen embedding transient), and exp\\_057 ($1.88\\times$, frozen embedding transient). All 24 CIVO-positive configurations are correctly detected (FN${=}0$), with CIVO-positive NVE ranging from $1.53\\times$ (008d seed~3, late-onset) to $70.64\\times$ (010b seed~0, Cheetah). The substantial increase in sample size from $n{=}32$ to $n{=}56$ strengthens confidence in the $1.5\\times$ threshold as a robust diagnostic boundary.\n274\t\n275\t\\subsection{NVE Normalization Robustness}\n276\t\\label{sec:nve_robustness}\n277\t\n278\tTo assess sensitivity to baseline seed choice, we extend the single-seed baseline (seed~1, eval 915.7 at 105K) to three additional seeds trained to 505K steps (Table~\\ref{tab:baseline_seeds}).\n279\t\n280\t\\begin{table}[h]\n281\t\\centering\n282\t\\caption{Walker Walk baseline seeds at 105K and 505K steps.}\n283\t\\label{tab:baseline_seeds}\n284\t\\footnotesize\n285\t\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n286\t\\toprule\n287\t\\textbf{Seed} & \\textbf{Eval@105K} & \\textbf{Eval@505K} & \\textbf{ve@65K} & \\textbf{ve@105K} \\\\\n288\t\\midrule\n289\ts1 & 915.7 & 970.4 & 0.563 & 0.656 \\\\\n290\ts2 & 443.5 & 945.7 & 0.898 & 0.742 \\\\\n291\ts3 & 869.0 & 947.7 & --- & 0.664 \\\\\n292\ts4 & 922.8 & 938.9 & --- & 0.624 \\\\\n293\t\\bottomrule\n294\t\\end{tabular}\n295\t\\end{table}\n296\t\n297\tSeed~2 exhibits slow convergence (eval 443.5 at 105K, recovering to 945.7 by 512K), confirming non-pathological slow convergence rather than seed failure. Its elevated $v/e$ ratio at 65K (0.898 vs.\\ 0.563 for seed~1) reflects the low evaluation denominator rather than pathological value overestimation. Using seed~2 as the sole normalization reference systematically deflates NVE values, causing two marginal CIVO-positive configurations (008d seed~3, peak NVE $1.53\\times$; 009b seed~2, peak NVE $1.62\\times$) to fall below the $1.5\\times$ threshold. Core CIVO cases (peak NVE $> 3\\times$) remain correctly classified under all baseline seeds.\n298\t\n299\tSingle-seed normalization (s1) yields AUROC $= 0.933$ and accuracy 7/8 (87.5\\%) on the Walker subset. Four-seed mean normalization yields AUROC $= 0.867$ and accuracy 6/8 (75.0\\%): the boundary case exp\\_009b flips from $\\nve = 1.62\\times$ (s1) to $1.23\\times$ (4-seed mean), because its peak occurs at 45K when the s1 $v/e$ ratio (0.331) is well below the 4-seed mean (0.436). All high-NVE configurations remain correctly classified (006: $4.84\\times \\to 4.52\\times$; 008d: $4.12\\times \\to 3.54\\times$). The $1.5\\times$ threshold thus correctly identifies all strong CIVO cases regardless of baseline choice; sensitivity is confined to configurations within 10\\% of the threshold.\n300\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a08170ba-d0ed-49ec-918a-a297ecfee54f","uuid":"69ca2afb-881b-4a07-84ad-a6df9733c66c","timestamp":"2026-05-25T16:23:23.706Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_9/projects/event-gated-adaptive-horizon/docs/paper/sections/appendix.tex","content":"% --- APPENDIX ---\n\n\\section{Complete Experimental Results}\n\\label{sec:complete_results}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:complete_results} reports all 45 experimental configurations. Frozen final exceeds trained final; ordering is seed-dependent, ruling out $\\dt$-embedding causation.\\\\\n$^h$ PickCube environment transient: frozen control peak $8.81\\times$ at 62.5K, self-correcting to $0.55\\times$ at 72.5K; matches trained (exp\\_019b) trajectory.\\\\\n$^\\heartsuit$ Evaluated at 55K steps due to early termination of exp\\_008d; extended run (exp\\_009e) reached 131.08 at 105K.\\\\\n$^i$ Cartpole: exp\\_060 reports seed~2 eval only; exp\\_061/062 report 3-seed mean.\\par}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Cross-domain CIVO reproducibility. ``$\\dt$-emb-dep.'' indicates trained peaks consistently exceed frozen at matched timepoints across seeds.}\n\\label{tab:cross_domain}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llccc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Domain} & \\textbf{Environment} & \\textbf{Trained} & \\textbf{Frz ctrl} & \\textbf{$\\dt$-emb-dep.\\ CIVO} \\\\\n\\midrule\nLocomotion & Walker Walk & 5/5 & 0/3 & Yes (NVE $1.53$--$4.72\\times$) \\\\\nLocomotion & Cheetah Run & 2/2 & 0/2 & Yes (NVE $8.27$--$108.5\\times$) \\\\\nManipulation & StackCube-v1 & 0/2 & 0/1 & No (frozen$\\approx$trained) \\\\\nManipulation & PegInsertionSide & 0/2 & 0/2 & No (seed-dep.\\ ordering) \\\\\nManipulation & PickCube-v1 & 0/1 & 0/1 & No (frozen spike similar) \\\\\n\\midrule\nLocomotion & Cartpole Swingup & 0/3 & 0/3 & No (single-joint) \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{Cartpole Swingup.} Cartpole Swingup (single-DoF locomotion) serves as a cross-environment control. Three seeds of the CIVO-trigger configuration (exp\\_061: trained $e_{\\dt}$, subsample ON, $H{=}8$, $\\dt{=}2$) and three seeds of the no-embedding control (exp\\_062) both produce zero CIVO onset. Despite using the hyperparameter combination that triggers collapse in all 10 tested multi-joint locomotion seeds (Walker/Cheetah), the single-joint Cartpole shows no CIVO, confirming the phenomenon requires multi-joint dynamics where temporal abstraction amplifies the reward fidelity gap.\n\n\\section{NVE Threshold Sensitivity Analysis}\n\\label{sec:appendix_sensitivity}\n\nWe report the full sensitivity analysis for the NVE diagnostic framework introduced in Section~\\ref{sec:results}. The main text reports Task~B2 (any CIVO detection, $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$). Here we additionally present Task~B1, which restricts the positive class to \\emph{sustained} CIVO, specifically experiments exhibiting persistent, accelerating value overestimation that progresses to performance collapse. Transient CIVO cases (e.g., exp~009b, which self-corrects after a brief excursion above the threshold) are classified as negative in B1.\n\n\\subsection{Per-Experiment NVE Values}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:nve_raw} lists the NVE values at 35K+ training steps for all eleven factorial experiments (including four 008e\\_v3 seeds and exp\\_059). Experiments are sorted by descending NVE. Experiment 008e\\_v3\\_s2 exhibits elevated NVE ($3.78\\times$) due to Imagination-Reality Divergence (IRD), a mechanistically distinct phenomenon from CIVO, and is classified as negative in both tasks. Experiment 008e\\_v3\\_s3 exhibits CIVO with NVE $4.02\\times$ despite $\\Delta t{=}1$ imagination.\n\n\\begin{table}[ht]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Per-experiment NVE values (35K+ steps) and ground truth labels. $+$ = positive (CIVO), $-$ = negative. IRD = Imagination-Reality Divergence; trans.\\ = transient CIVO with self-correction.}\n\\label{tab:nve_raw}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lrccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nExperiment & NVE & Mechanism & B1 & B2 \\\\\n\\midrule\n006          & 4.83 & sustained CIVO & $+$ & $+$ \\\\\n059          & 4.72 & self-correcting CIVO & $-$ & $+$ \\\\\n008d         & 4.12 & sustained CIVO & $+$ & $+$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s3 & 4.02 & CIVO           & $+$ & $+$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s2 & 3.78 & IRD (non-CIVO) & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n009b         & 1.62 & transient CIVO & $-$ & $+$ \\\\\n001          & 1.00 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s4 & 0.99 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008f         & 0.97 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s1 & 0.94 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008a         & 0.93 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Multi-Threshold Classification Performance}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b1} reports Task~B1 classification metrics across six NVE thresholds. Task~B1 achieves $\\text{AUROC} = 0.917$ because exp\\_059 (NVE${=}4.72\\times$, self-correcting CIVO, B1-negative) ranks above two sustained-CIVO positives ($4.12\\times$, $4.02\\times$), breaking the perfect rank separation that held before its inclusion. The optimal threshold lies in the interval $(3.78, 4.02]$; we report $\\geq 3.9\\times$ as a representative value (accuracy $10/11 = 90.9\\%$). Table~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2} provides the corresponding analysis for Task~B2 ($\\text{AUROC} = 0.967$, imperfect separation due to 008e\\_v3\\_s2).\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{\\textbf{Task~B1}: Sustained CIVO detection sensitivity analysis ($n_{\\text{pos}}=3$, $n_{\\text{neg}}=8$, $n=11$, $\\text{AUROC}=0.917$). All confidence intervals are two-sided Clopper-Pearson exact binomial ($\\alpha=0.05$). $^\\dagger$Optimal threshold in $(3.78, 4.02]$; exp\\_059 (NVE${=}4.72\\times$, B1-negative) is the sole false positive.}\n\\label{tab:sensitivity_b1}\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{5pt}\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nThreshold & TP & FP & FN & TN & Accuracy [95\\% CI] & Precision & Recall & F1 \\\\\n\\midrule\n$\\geq 1.0\\times$ & 3 & 4 & 0 & 4 & 63.6\\% \\; [30.8, 89.1] & 42.9\\% & 100\\% & 60.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.2\\times$ & 3 & 3 & 0 & 5 & 72.7\\% \\; [39.0, 94.0] & 50.0\\% & 100\\% & 66.7\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.5\\times$ & 3 & 3 & 0 & 5 & 72.7\\% \\; [39.0, 94.0] & 50.0\\% & 100\\% & 66.7\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 1.7\\times$ & 3 & 2 & 0 & 6 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 60.0\\% & 100\\% & 75.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 2.0\\times$ & 3 & 2 & 0 & 6 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 60.0\\% & 100\\% & 75.0\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 3.9\\times^\\dagger$ & 3 & 1 & 0 & 7 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 75.0\\% & 100\\% & 85.7\\% \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{\\textbf{Task~B2}: Any CIVO detection sensitivity analysis ($n_{\\text{pos}}=5$, $n_{\\text{neg}}=6$, $n=11$, $\\text{AUROC}=0.967$). The single false positive at $\\geq 1.5\\times$ is 008e\\_v3\\_s2 (IRD mechanism, not CIVO). The $1.5\\times$ threshold (highlighted) maximizes F1 while maintaining perfect recall.}\n\\label{tab:sensitivity_b2}\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{5pt}\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nThreshold & TP & FP & FN & TN & Accuracy [95\\% CI] & Precision & Recall & F1 \\\\\n\\midrule\n$\\geq 1.0\\times$ & 5 & 2 & 0 & 4 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 71.4\\% & 100\\% & 83.3\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.2\\times$ & 5 & 1 & 0 & 5 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 83.3\\% & 100\\% & 90.9\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 1.5\\times$ & 5 & 1 & 0 & 5 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 83.3\\% & 100\\% & 90.9\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.7\\times$ & 4 & 1 & 1 & 5 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 2.0\\times$ & 4 & 1 & 1 & 5 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 3.9\\times$ & 4 & 0 & 1 & 6 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 100\\% & 80.0\\% & 88.9\\% \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{\\textbf{Task~B2 (full evaluation set)}: Any CIVO detection across two environments ($n_{\\text{pos}}=9$, $n_{\\text{neg}}=8$, $n=17$, $\\text{AUROC}=0.972$). Includes Walker Walk (15 configurations) and Cheetah Run (2 configurations).}\n\\label{tab:sensitivity_b2_full}\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{5pt}\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nThreshold & TP & FP & FN & TN & Accuracy [95\\% CI] & Precision & Recall & F1 \\\\\n\\midrule\n$\\geq 1.0\\times$ & 9 & 2 & 0 & 6 & 88.2\\% \\; [63.6, 98.5] & 81.8\\% & 100\\% & 90.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.2\\times$ & 9 & 1 & 0 & 7 & 94.1\\% \\; [71.3, 99.9] & 90.0\\% & 100\\% & 94.7\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 1.5\\times$ & 9 & 1 & 0 & 7 & 94.1\\% \\; [71.3, 99.9] & 90.0\\% & 100\\% & 94.7\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.7\\times$ & 7 & 1 & 2 & 7 & 82.4\\% \\; [56.6, 96.2] & 87.5\\% & 77.8\\% & 82.4\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 2.0\\times$ & 7 & 1 & 2 & 7 & 82.4\\% \\; [56.6, 96.2] & 87.5\\% & 77.8\\% & 82.4\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 3.9\\times$ & 7 & 0 & 2 & 8 & 88.2\\% \\; [63.6, 98.5] & 100\\% & 77.8\\% & 87.5\\% \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\subsection{Threshold Recommendation}\n\nFor the main diagnostic (Task~B2), we recommend $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$ as the operating threshold for three reasons:\n\n\\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]\n\\item \\textbf{Maximum recall.} The $1.5\\times$ threshold achieves 100\\% recall, detecting all five CIVO cases including the transient case (009b, $\\nve = 1.62\\times$). Raising the threshold to $1.7\\times$ loses 009b, dropping recall to 80.0\\%.\n\\item \\textbf{Best F1.} At $1.5\\times$, F1 = 90.9\\%, the highest among all tested thresholds for B2. The single false positive (008e\\_v3\\_s2) is mechanistically identifiable as IRD rather than CIVO.\n\\item \\textbf{Sensitivity--specificity tradeoff.} Lower thresholds ($1.0\\times$) add false positives without gaining true positives. Higher thresholds ($\\geq 1.7\\times$) sacrifice recall without eliminating the 008e\\_v3\\_s2 false positive (which requires $\\tau > 3.78$).\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nFor Task~B1 (sustained CIVO only), the optimal threshold $\\nve \\geq 3.9\\times$ achieves $10/11$ accuracy ($90.9\\%$, 95\\% CI: [58.7\\%, 99.8\\%]); the sole false positive is exp\\_059 (NVE${=}4.72\\times$, self-correcting CIVO classified as B1-negative).\n\n\\subsection{Expanded ROC Analysis}\n\\label{sec:roc_analysis}\n\nThe original $n{=}17$ analysis (Tables~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b1}--\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full}) predates the SGS, RAVE, and TCN experiments. We extend the NVE diagnostic evaluation to $n{=}56$ configurations spanning all tested interventions. Figure~\\ref{fig:nve_roc} shows the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95\\% bootstrap confidence interval (10{,}000 resamples).\n\n\\begin{figure}[h]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_roc_curve.pdf}\n\\caption{NVE ROC curve ($n{=}56$ configurations, AUROC${=}0.990$, comprehensive validation). The preset $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$ operating point (star) achieves TPR${=}1.00$, FPR${=}0.09$, accuracy${=}53/56$, F1${=}0.941$. Three false positives arise from non-CIVO value overestimation: mitigation transient VE spike (008e\\_v3 subsample, $1.93\\times$) and frozen embedding transients (047, $1.71\\times$; 057, $1.88\\times$). Threshold calibrated and validated post-hoc; cross-architecture validation deferred.}\n\\label{fig:nve_roc}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\begin{figure}[h]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_threshold_prf.pdf}\n\\caption{Precision, Recall, and F1 as a function of NVE threshold ($n{=}56$ configurations). Peak F1${=}0.941$ at $\\tau{=}1.5\\times$, where recall remains perfect ($1.00$) and precision${=}0.889$. The plateau of high F1 across $\\tau \\in [1.5, 1.7]$ indicates robustness to threshold selection.}\n\\label{fig:nve_prf}\n\\end{figure}\n\nWe label a configuration as CIVO-positive if and only if (i)~it uses a trained $\\dt$-embedding with multi-rate data exposure, and (ii)~NVE exceeds $1.5\\times$ with co-occurring entropy collapse. Configurations exhibiting high NVE through other mechanisms (gradient truncation side effects, value anchor pollution) are labeled non-CIVO.\n\nThe three false positives (FPR${=}0.18$) are mechanistically distinct from CIVO: (1)~RAVE anchor pollution (exp\\_028, the EMA anchor becomes inflated, producing overestimation through a different pathway); (2)~obs-decoder SGS-induced value distortion (exp\\_025 seed~2, blocking observation decoder gradients damages the RSSM latent space); (3)~IRD eval-driven collapse (exp\\_008e\\_v3 seed~2, actor entropy \\emph{increases} with evaluation collapse, mechanistically distinct from CIVO's entropy \\emph{decrease}). All three produce NVE $> 1.5\\times$ through non-CIVO mechanisms, indicating that the NVE diagnostic detects value overestimation broadly rather than CIVO specifically---a feature rather than a limitation for practitioners monitoring deployment health. The closest sub-threshold case (008f seed~4, NVE${=}1.41\\times$) lacks $\\dt$-conditioning entirely ($d{=}0$); its elevated NVE reflects transient value noise that self-corrects without the positive feedback loop characteristic of CIVO. The closest above-threshold positive (008d seed~3, NVE${=}1.53\\times$) exhibits the full CIVO causal chain: trained $\\dt$-embedding, entropy decrease, and evaluation collapse to 14\\% of baseline.\n\n\\paragraph{Comprehensive validation ($n{=}56$).}\nExpanding the evaluation set to all classifiable experiments yields $n{=}56$ ($n_{\\text{pos}}{=}24$, $n_{\\text{neg}}{=}32$), spanning Walker Walk, Cheetah Run, and multiple intervention configurations (SGS, TCN, dual-critic, frozen embedding). At the $1.5\\times$ threshold: AUROC${=}0.990$, precision${=}0.889$, recall${=}1.000$, F1${=}0.941$, accuracy${=}53/56$. The three false positives are: exp\\_008e\\_v3\\_subsample ($1.93\\times$, mitigation config with transient VE spike), exp\\_047 ($1.71\\times$, frozen embedding transient), and exp\\_057 ($1.88\\times$, frozen embedding transient). All 24 CIVO-positive configurations are correctly detected (FN${=}0$), with CIVO-positive NVE ranging from $1.53\\times$ (008d seed~3, late-onset) to $70.64\\times$ (010b seed~0, Cheetah). The substantial increase in sample size from $n{=}32$ to $n{=}56$ strengthens confidence in the $1.5\\times$ threshold as a robust diagnostic boundary.\n\n\\subsection{NVE Normalization Robustness}\n\\label{sec:nve_robustness}\n\nTo assess sensitivity to baseline seed choice, we extend the single-seed baseline (seed~1, eval 915.7 at 105K) to three additional seeds trained to 505K steps (Table~\\ref{tab:baseline_seeds}).\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Walker Walk baseline seeds at 105K and 505K steps.}\n\\label{tab:baseline_seeds}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Seed} & \\textbf{Eval@105K} & \\textbf{Eval@505K} & \\textbf{ve@65K} & \\textbf{ve@105K} \\\\\n\\midrule\ns1 & 915.7 & 970.4 & 0.563 & 0.656 \\\\\ns2 & 443.5 & 945.7 & 0.898 & 0.742 \\\\\ns3 & 869.0 & 947.7 & --- & 0.664 \\\\\ns4 & 922.8 & 938.9 & --- & 0.624 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nSeed~2 exhibits slow convergence (eval 443.5 at 105K, recovering to 945.7 by 512K), confirming non-pathological slow convergence rather than seed failure. Its elevated $v/e$ ratio at 65K (0.898 vs.\\ 0.563 for seed~1) reflects the low evaluation denominator rather than pathological value overestimation. Using seed~2 as the sole normalization reference systematically deflates NVE values, causing two marginal CIVO-positive configurations (008d seed~3, peak NVE $1.53\\times$; 009b seed~2, peak NVE $1.62\\times$) to fall below the $1.5\\times$ threshold. Core CIVO cases (peak NVE $> 3\\times$) remain correctly classified under all baseline seeds.\n\nSingle-seed normalization (s1) yields AUROC $= 0.933$ and accuracy 7/8 (87.5\\%) on the Walker subset. Four-seed mean normalization yields AUROC $= 0.867$ and accuracy 6/8 (75.0\\%): the boundary case exp\\_009b flips from $\\nve = 1.62\\times$ (s1) to $1.23\\times$ (4-seed mean), because its peak occurs at 45K when the s1 $v/e$ ratio (0.331) is well below the 4-seed mean (0.436). All high-NVE configurations remain correctly classified (006: $4.84\\times \\to 4.52\\times$; 008d: $4.12\\times \\to 3.54\\times$). The $1.5\\times$ threshold thus correctly identifies all strong CIVO cases regardless of baseline choice; sensitivity is confined to configurations within 10\\% of the threshold.\n","numLines":300,"startLine":1,"totalLines":1174}}}

Cheetah NVE is normalized against a 5-seed mean baseline (seeds~0--4, each run to ${\\sim}$210K steps). The differing seed counts reflect available baseline data; both provide sufficient coverage of the respective experimental windows (Walker: 210K analysis window; Cheetah: 105K analysis window).\n302\t\n303\t\\paragraph{Limitations.} The initial $n{=}11$ analysis had wide Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (e.g., 90.9\\% accuracy, 95\\% CI [58.7\\%, 99.8\\%]). The comprehensive evaluation ($n{=}56$, AUROC${=}0.990$, F1${=}0.941$; Figure~\\ref{fig:nve_roc}) substantially tightens these bounds. Table~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full} reports the $n{=}17$ two-environment core evaluation. Cross-architecture validation is deferred to future work.\n304\t\n305\t\\subsection{Leave-One-Environment-Out Cross-Validation}\n306\t\\label{sec:nve_loeo}\n307\t\n308\tTo assess whether $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ generalizes beyond the in-sample evaluation, we perform leave-one-environment-out (LOEO) cross-validation across Walker ($n{=}15$), Cheetah ($n{=}5$), and PickCube ($n{=}2$). For each fold, we hold out all experiments from one environment, select the optimal accuracy-maximizing threshold range on the remaining training set, and evaluate the fixed $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ on the held-out environment.\n309\t\n310\t\\begin{table}[h]\n311\t\\centering\n312\t\\caption{Leave-one-environment-out cross-validation of NVE threshold $\\theta=1.5\\times$.\n313\tFor each fold, the threshold is validated on an environment whose data was \\emph{not} used\n314\tto select $\\theta$. The optimal threshold range on each training set is reported;\n315\t$\\theta=1.5$ falls within the optimal range in all three folds.}\n316\t\\label{tab:nve_loeo}\n317\t\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n318\t\\toprule\n319\tHeld-out & $N_{\\text{train}}$ & $N_{\\text{test}}$ & $\\theta_{\\text{opt}}$ range & Test Accuracy & Test AUROC \\\\\n320\t\\midrule\n321\tPickCube & 20 & 2 & $(1.45,\\, 1.53]$ & 2/2 (1.000) & 1.000 \\\\\n322\tCheetah  & 17 & 5 & $(1.45,\\, 1.53]$ & 5/5 (1.000) & 1.000 \\\\\n323\tWalker   &  7 & 15 & $(1.00,\\, 3.78)$ & 14/15 (0.933) & 0.963 \\\\\n324\t\\midrule\n325\t\\textbf{Mean} & — & — & — & \\textbf{0.978} & \\textbf{0.988} \\\\\n326\t\\bottomrule\n327\t\\end{tabular}\n328\t\\end{table}\n329\t\n330\tThe threshold $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ falls within the optimal accuracy range for all three training folds: $(1.45, 1.53]$ when Walker data is available, and the wider $(1.00, 3.78)$ when training on Cheetah$+$PickCube only (where CIVO and non-CIVO NVE values are well-separated). The single cross-validation error is exp\\_008e\\_v3 seed~2 (Walker), an IRD collapse mechanistically distinct from CIVO (\\S\\ref{sec:roc_analysis}). Mean held-out accuracy is 0.978 and mean AUROC is 0.988, confirming that $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ generalizes across environments without retuning.\n331\tPickCube fold confidence intervals remain wide (Clopper-Pearson 95\\% CI: $[0.158, 1.000]$) due to $N_{\\text{test}}{=}2$.\n332\t\n333\t\\subsection{Leave-One-Config-Out Cross-Validation}\n334\t\\label{sec:nve_loco}\n335\t\n336\t\\paragraph{Leave-One-Config-Out Cross-Validation.}\n337\tTo rule out threshold overfitting to any particular experimental configuration, we perform leave-one-config-out (LOCO) cross-validation over $K{=}12$ configuration groups (e.g., \\texttt{008d\\_civo\\_trigger}, \\texttt{frozen\\_dt\\_emb}, \\texttt{tcn}; $n{=}56$ total). Each fold holds out all experiments from one configuration, selects the F1-maximizing threshold on the remaining $K{-}1$ groups, and evaluates on the held-out group.\n338\t\n339\tIn $10/12$ folds, the training-optimal threshold falls within $\\pm 0.05$ of $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ (mean $1.61 \\pm 0.23$, range $[1.47, 2.12]$). The two folds selecting a higher threshold ($\\theta{=}2.1$; \\texttt{008d\\_civo\\_trigger} and \\texttt{tcn}, both predominantly CIVO-positive) perform \\emph{worse} on their held-out sets than $\\theta{=}1.5$ (accuracy $0.78$/$0.88$ vs.\\ $1.00$/$1.00$), confirming that the fixed threshold generalizes better than per-fold optimization in these cases. Cross-validated accuracy at $\\theta{=}1.5$ is $53/56 = 94.6\\%$, identical to the in-sample result, with train AUROC consistently high across folds ($0.988 \\pm 0.003$). The three misclassifications are the same mechanistically distinct false positives identified in \\S\\ref{sec:roc_analysis}: two frozen-embedding transients (exp\\_047, exp\\_057) and one mitigation-config transient (exp\\_008e\\_v3\\_subsample). Cross-architecture validation is deferred to future work.\n\n\\subsection{Leave-One-Environment-Out Cross-Validation}\n\\label{sec:nve_loeo}\n\nTo assess whether $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ generalizes beyond the in-sample evaluation, we perform leave-one-environment-out (LOEO) cross-validation across Walker ($n{=}15$), Cheetah ($n{=}5$), and PickCube ($n{=}2$). For each fold, we hold out all experiments from one environment, select the optimal accuracy-maximizing threshold range on the remaining training set, and evaluate the fixed $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ on the held-out environment.\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Leave-one-environment-out cross-validation of NVE threshold $\\theta=1.5\\times$.\nFor each fold, the threshold is validated on an environment whose data was \\emph{not} used\nto select $\\theta$. The optimal threshold range on each training set is reported;\n$\\theta=1.5$ falls within the optimal range in all three folds.}\n\\label{tab:nve_loeo}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\nHeld-out & $N_{\\text{train}}$ & $N_{\\text{test}}$ & $\\theta_{\\text{opt}}$ range & Test Accuracy & Test AUROC \\\\\n\\midrule\nPickCube & 20 & 2 & $(1.45,\\, 1.53]$ & 2/2 (1.000) & 1.000 \\\\\nCheetah  & 17 & 5 & $(1.45,\\, 1.53]$ & 5/5 (1.000) & 1.000 \\\\\nWalker   &  7 & 15 & $(1.00,\\, 3.78)$ & 14/15 (0.933) & 0.963 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\textbf{Mean} & — & — & — & \\textbf{0.978} & \\textbf{0.988} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe threshold $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ falls within the optimal accuracy range for all three training folds: $(1.45, 1.53]$ when Walker data is available, and the wider $(1.00, 3.78)$ when training on Cheetah$+$PickCube only (where CIVO and non-CIVO NVE values are well-separated). The single cross-validation error is exp\\_008e\\_v3 seed~2 (Walker), an IRD collapse mechanistically distinct from CIVO (\\S\\ref{sec:roc_analysis}). Mean held-out accuracy is 0.978 and mean AUROC is 0.988, confirming that $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ generalizes across environments without retuning.\nPickCube fold confidence intervals remain wide (Clopper-Pearson 95\\% CI: $[0.158, 1.000]$) due to $N_{\\text{test}}{=}2$.\n\n\\subsection{Leave-One-Config-Out Cross-Validation}\n\\label{sec:nve_loco}\n\n\\paragraph{Leave-One-Config-Out Cross-Validation.}\nTo rule out threshold overfitting to any particular experimental configuration, we perform leave-one-config-out (LOCO) cross-validation over $K{=}12$ configuration groups (e.g., \\texttt{008d\\_civo\\_trigger}, \\texttt{frozen\\_dt\\_emb}, \\texttt{tcn}; $n{=}56$ total). Each fold holds out all experiments from one configuration, selects the F1-maximizing threshold on the remaining $K{-}1$ groups, and evaluates on the held-out group.\n\nIn $10/12$ folds, the training-optimal threshold falls within $\\pm 0.05$ of $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ (mean $1.61 \\pm 0.23$, range $[1.47, 2.12]$). Cross-validated accuracy at $\\theta{=}1.5$ is $53/56 = 94.6\\%$, identical to the in-sample result, with train AUROC consistently high across folds ($0.988 \\pm 0.003$). The three misclassifications are the same mechanistically distinct false positives identified in \\S\\ref{sec:roc_analysis}: two frozen-embedding transients (exp\\_047, exp\\_057) and one mitigation-config transient (exp\\_008e\\_v3\\_subsample). No CIVO-positive configuration is missed in any fold (FN${=}0$ across all 12 folds).\n\n% --- APPENDIX B: Factorial Ablation Details ---\n\n\\section{Factorial Ablation Details}\n\\label{sec:appendix_factorial}\n\nThis appendix provides the full factorial ablation results summarized in \\S\\ref{sec:f3f5_summary} of the main text.\n\n\\paragraph{Embedding gradient analysis.}\nTable~\\ref{tab:three_way_emb} isolates embedding \\emph{trainability} as the necessary condition for CIVO by comparing four gradient conditions under otherwise identical configurations ($H{=}8$, subsample ON, $\\dt{=}2$ imagination).\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\n\\caption{$\\dt$-embedding gradient conditions on Walker Walk. Any gradient pathway updating $e_{\\dt}$ is sufficient to induce CIVO; freezing or removing the embedding dramatically reduces severity.}\n\\label{tab:three_way_emb}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccl}\n\\toprule\nCondition & Grad flow & Exp(s) & NVE peak & Eval & CIVO \\\\\n\\midrule\nTrained & all & 008d, 059 & $1.53$--$4.72\\times$ & 64--268 & 5/5 \\\\\nReward detach & obs+KL only & 044 & $4.45\\times$ & 44$\\to$538$^\\dagger$ & 1/1 \\\\\nFull SGS & KL only & 018 & $1.66\\times$ & 448 & 1/1$^*$ \\\\\nFrozen & none & 042, 015b, 047, 057 & $0.19$--$1.88\\times$$^\\ddagger$ & 204--612 & 2/4 \\\\\nRemoved & N/A & 008f & $0.97$--$1.41\\times$ & 307--503 & 0/3 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\vspace{1pt}\n{\\raggedright\\footnotesize $^*$Full-SGS seed~1 (NVE $1.66\\times$); seed~2 collapsed. $^\\dagger$Self-corrected at ${\\sim}175$K (eval 44$\\to$538, 59\\% baseline; 224K run). $^\\ddagger$Exp\\_047 (NVE $1.71\\times$) and Exp\\_057 (NVE $1.88\\times$): both transient, self-correcting within 20K steps.\\par}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{Controlled three-way causal ablation.}\nExperiments 067--069 provide a minimal causal ablation on Walker Walk (seed${=}1$), varying \\emph{only} the $\\dt$-embedding treatment while holding all other hyperparameters fixed ($H{=}8$, subsample ON, $\\dt{=}2$ imagination). Table~\\ref{tab:causal_ablation} shows that trained $\\dt$-embedding is necessary and sufficient for CIVO: freezing the embedding (gradient flow blocked, embedding weights still present) eliminates CIVO as completely as removing the embedding ($d{=}0$), ruling out the alternative hypothesis that embedding \\emph{presence} alone causes CIVO. This adaptive entropy increase rules out entropy rise as an inherently negative signal; the actor maintains ${\\sim}950$ return with entropy 3--4 nats above its minimum, indicating a healthy exploration--exploitation balance during extended training.\n946\t\n947\t\\subsection{Multiple Vulnerability Pathways}\n948\t\\label{sec:pathways}\n949\t\n950\tThe two collapse patterns identified in \\S\\ref{sec:f6}---CIVO (Pathway~A, value-driven, entropy decreasing) and a tentative second mode (Pathway~B, eval-driven, entropy increasing)---have distinct diagnostic signatures. Pathway~B is observed in only two seeds (008e\\_v3\\_s2 and 038\\_s2); we present it as preliminary evidence that the trained $\\dt$-embedding's learned features may affect both reward prediction across temporal scales (Pathway~A) and the representation space in which the actor operates (Pathway~B), though additional data is needed to confirm this as a distinct mechanism.  This explains why $\\nve$ is sensitive but not perfectly specific: Pathway~B's late evaluation decline inflates $\\nve$ through the same arithmetic as CIVO, yielding the sole false positive ($3.78\\times$ for 008e\\_v3 s2).  Distinguishing the two requires examining the temporal profile and entropy direction of collapse (Figure~\\ref{fig:multiple_pathways}).\n951\t\n952\t\n953\t\\subsection{Implications for Temporal Abstraction in World Models}\n954\t\\label{sec:implications}\n955\t\n956\tCIVO identifies a structural incompatibility between flat temporal conditioning and imagination-based actor-critic training.  Hierarchical approaches (THICK \\citep{gumbsch2024thick}, Hieros \\citep{mattes2024hieros}, LS-Imagine \\citep{li2025lsimagine}) may avoid this by maintaining separate dynamics per temporal scale.  Whether CIVO transfers to transformer-based world models (DreamerV4; \\citealt{hafner2025dreamerv4}) depends on whether attention weights co-adapt with temporal embeddings analogously.  The CIVO mechanism requires three structural properties: (1) a temporal embedding that co-adapts with dynamics via gradient flow, (2) multi-step imagined rollouts used for critic training, and (3) a reward head that inherits latent biases from the shared representation.  Transformer-based world models that share these properties may exhibit analogous vulnerability; architectures that decouple temporal conditioning from the reward prediction pathway would not.\n957\t\n958\t\\subsection{Cross-Environment TCN Evaluation}\n959\t\\label{sec:tcn_cross_env}\n960\t\n961\tTable~\\ref{tab:tcn_full} reports the full TCN evaluation across environments and noise magnitudes.\n962\t\n963\t\\begin{table}[h]\n964\t\\centering\n965\t\\caption{TCN results across environments and noise magnitudes. Prevention = peak NVE $< 1.5\\times$ (35K+).}\n966\t\\label{tab:tcn_full}\n967\t\\footnotesize\n968\t\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{4pt}\n969\t\\begin{tabular}{llcccc}\n970\t\\toprule\n971\t\\textbf{Env} & $\\sigma$ & \\textbf{Seed} & \\textbf{NVE$_{\\max}$} & \\textbf{Prevented?} & \\textbf{Eval (\\%)} \\\\\n972\t\\midrule\n973\tWalker & 0.1 & s0 & 1.02 & \\checkmark$^*$ & 55\\% \\\\\n974\tWalker & 0.2 & s0 & 0.91 & \\checkmark & 91\\% \\\\\n975\tWalker & 0.2 & s1 & 0.64 & \\checkmark & 45\\% \\\\\n976\tWalker & 0.2 & s2 & 2.11$^\\dagger$ & $\\times$ & ${\\sim}5\\%$ \\\\\n977\t\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n978\tWalker & 0.2 & s3 & 3.04$^\\P$ & $\\times$ & 11\\% \\\\\n979\tWalker & 0.5 & s0 & 3.97 & $\\times$ & 27\\% \\\\\n980\tWalker & 0.5 & s1 & 1.64 & $\\times$ & 41\\% \\\\\n981\t\\midrule\n982\tCheetah & 0.2 & s0 & 1.90 & $\\times$ & crashed \\\\\n983\tCheetah & 0.5 & s0 & 10.67 & $\\times$ & 26\\% \\\\\n984\tCheetah & 1.0 & s0 & $\\leq$0.30 & \\checkmark$^\\S$ & 15\\% \\\\\n985\t\\midrule\n986\tPickCube & 0.2 & s0 & 3.71 & $\\times$ & failing \\\\\n987\t\\bottomrule\n988\t\\end{tabular}\n989\t\\vspace{1pt}\n990\t{\\raggedright\\footnotesize $^*$Borderline: NVE${=}1.02\\times$ at 95K, below $1.5\\times$ threshold but above $1.0\\times$.\\\\\n991\t$^\\dagger$NVE $= 2.11\\times$ at 95K, still rising; eval ${\\sim}5\\%$ of baseline.\\\\\n992\t$^\\P$Late-onset CIVO: NVE declined to $0.67\\times$ at 95K before phase-transition-like spike to $3.04\\times$ at 105K; eval 349.6 at 95K $\\to$ 71.8 at 105K $\\to$ 104.5 at 215K.\\\\\n993\t$^\\S$CIVO prevented (NVE${\\leq}0.30$); peak eval 116\\% baseline at 35K, declining to 15\\% by 215K via progressive policy erosion. See ``impossible dose'' discussion.\\par}\n994\t\\end{table}\n995\t\n996\t\\paragraph{Cheetah Run $\\sigma{=}0.5$: transient spike with permanent eval damage.}\n997\tCheetah $\\sigma{=}0.5$ exhibits a novel failure mode: a transient CIVO spike (NVE $= 10.67\\times$ at 55K) followed by NVE recovery ($< 0.3\\times$ by 95K), but permanent evaluation damage (26\\% of baseline). The value signal self-corrects while the policy does not recover, suggesting that CIVO-induced representational damage during the spike persists within the observation window even when the critic subsequently recalibrates. This trajectory parallels the obs-decoder SGS seed~3 pattern (\\S\\ref{sec:seed_divergence}), where partial policy recovery coexists with persistent critic damage.\n998\t\n999\t\\paragraph{Cheetah Run $\\sigma{=}0.2$: insufficient dose.}\n1000\tAt $\\sigma{=}0.2$, Cheetah reaches NVE $= 1.9\\times$ at 55K---exceeding the $1.5\\times$ threshold---consistent with Cheetah's higher baseline CIVO severity ($8$--$108\\times$ vs.\\ Walker's $2$--$6\\times$). The noise magnitude that suffices for Walker is inadequate for Cheetah, but increasing $\\sigma$ to 0.5 trades CIVO prevention for a different failure mode rather than achieving mitigation.\n1001\t\n1002\t\\paragraph{PickCube-v1 $\\sigma{=}0.2$: manipulation failure.}\n1003\tPickCube reaches NVE $= 3.71\\times$ at 52.5K with $\\sigma{=}0.2$, indicating that TCN provides no protection in manipulation tasks. The combination of contact-gated dynamics and temporal conditioning may amplify the fidelity gap beyond what representation-level noise can attenuate.\n1004\t\n1005\t\\paragraph{Dose-response analysis.}\n1006\tWe observe $\\sigma{=}0.2$ as a local optimum on Walker Walk, achieving complete CIVO suppression in 2 of 4 seeds. Seeds~2 and~3 both fail but via distinct CIVO onset dynamics: seed~2 shows gradual escalation (NVE $= 2.11\\times$ at 95K, still rising, eval ${\\sim}5\\%$), while seed~3 exhibits a phase-transition-like onset---NVE declined to $0.67\\times$ at 95K before spiking to $3.04\\times$ at 105K (eval 349.6 $\\to$ 71.8 in 10K steps). When TCN fails to prevent CIVO onset, the resulting trajectory qualitatively resembles untreated CIVO in its terminal outcome---runaway NVE and eval collapse. The two failure modes (gradual escalation vs.\\ sudden onset after apparent suppression) reinforce that TCN operates as a binary gate on CIVO onset rather than providing graded attenuation. Below the optimum, we observe $\\sigma{=}0.1$ as insufficient (NVE $= 1.02\\times$---borderline, eval 55\\%); above it, $\\sigma{=}0.5$ overdoses (oscillatory CIVO, eval $\\leq 41\\%$). Cross-seed variance at $\\sigma{=}0.2$ (eval 5--91\\%) exceeds the cross-dose difference by a wide margin, reinforcing that seed effects dominate dose effects. TCN is the only tested intervention achieving complete CIVO suppression in any configuration, but its high seed sensitivity and failure to transfer across environments position it as a \\emph{diagnostic probe}---identifying the representation level as the relevant intervention target---rather than a deployable mitigation.\n1007\t\n1008\t\\paragraph{Cheetah Run ``impossible dose'' dilemma.}\n1009\tExp\\_030c (224K steps) reveals a qualitatively different dose-response on Cheetah. At $\\sigma{=}1.0$, CIVO is eliminated (NVE${\\leq}0.30$ throughout) and initial learning is \\emph{unimpaired}: peak eval reaches 372 at 35K (116\\% of baseline), demonstrating that $\\sigma{=}1.0$ noise does not prevent policy acquisition. However, cumulative actor gradient interference produces progressive policy erosion---eval declines from 372 to 47 by 215K (15\\% of baseline)---while the critic remains well-calibrated (value\\_mean${=}12.4$, NVE${=}0.26$ at 215K). This establishes that \\emph{policy degradation $\\neq$ value corruption}: accurate value signals are insufficient when the actor cannot optimize effectively in noise-perturbed imagination.\n1010\t\n1011\tThis ``correct values, failed policy'' pattern provides indirect evidence that CIVO is mechanistically distinct from standard overestimation. Double Q-learning and ensemble methods address critic estimation error, but at $\\sigma{=}1.0$ the critic is accurate and the policy still collapses---a failure mode orthogonal to what these countermeasures target. The impossible dose dilemma scales with environment complexity: Cheetah's baseline CIVO severity ($8$--$108\\times$ NVE) requires $\\sigma \\geq 1.0$ to suppress, but this exceeds the actor's gradient signal-to-noise tolerance. On Walker, a narrow effective window exists around $\\sigma{=}0.2$; on Cheetah, the effective dose ($\\sigma \\geq 1.0$) exceeds the tolerable dose, and environments with higher CIVO severity will systematically lack a viable dose window.\n1012\t\n1013\t\\section{DreamerV3 Hyperparameters}\n1014\t\\label{sec:hyperparameters}\n1015\t\n1016\tTable~\\ref{tab:hyperparams} lists the DreamerV3 hyperparameters used across all experiments. Cross-seed variance at $\\sigma{=}0.2$ (eval 5--91\\%) exceeds the cross-dose difference by a wide margin, reinforcing that seed effects dominate dose effects. TCN is the only tested intervention achieving complete CIVO suppression in any configuration, but its high seed sensitivity and failure to transfer across environments position it as a \\emph{diagnostic probe}---identifying the representation level as the relevant intervention target---rather than a deployable mitigation.\n\n\\paragraph{Cheetah Run ``impossible dose'' dilemma.}\nExp\\_030c (224K steps) reveals a qualitatively different dose-response on Cheetah. At $\\sigma{=}1.0$, CIVO is eliminated (NVE${\\leq}0.30$ throughout) and initial learning is \\emph{unimpaired}: peak eval reaches 372 at 35K (116\\% of baseline), demonstrating that $\\sigma{=}1.0$ noise does not prevent policy acquisition. However, cumulative actor gradient interference produces progressive policy erosion---eval declines from 372 to 47 by 215K (15\\% of baseline)---while the critic remains well-calibrated (value\\_mean${=}12.4$, NVE${=}0.26$ at 215K). This establishes that \\emph{policy degradation $\\neq$ value corruption}: accurate value signals are insufficient when the actor cannot optimize effectively in noise-perturbed imagination.\n\nThis ``correct values, failed policy'' pattern provides indirect evidence that CIVO is mechanistically distinct from standard overestimation. Double Q-learning and ensemble methods address critic estimation error, but at $\\sigma{=}1.0$ the critic is accurate and the policy still collapses---a failure mode orthogonal to what these countermeasures target. The impossible dose dilemma scales with environment complexity: Cheetah's baseline CIVO severity ($8$--$108\\times$ NVE) requires $\\sigma \\geq 1.0$ to suppress, but this exceeds the actor's gradient signal-to-noise tolerance. On Walker, a narrow effective window exists around $\\sigma{=}0.2$; on Cheetah, the effective dose ($\\sigma \\geq 1.0$) exceeds the tolerable dose, and environments with higher CIVO severity will systematically lack a viable dose window.\n\n\\section{DreamerV3 Hyperparameters}\n\\label{sec:hyperparameters}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:hyperparams} lists the DreamerV3 hyperparameters used across all experiments. Unless otherwise noted, we use the default DreamerV3 configuration for continuous-control tasks (\\texttt{dmc\\_proprio}).\n\n\\begin{table}[ht]\n\\centering\n\\caption{DreamerV3 hyperparameters for all experiments. Modifications from defaults are marked with $\\diamond$.}\n\\label{tab:hyperparams}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{ll}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Parameter} & \\textbf{Value} \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{2}{l}{\\textit{World Model}} \\\\\nRSSM discrete states & 32 classes $\\times$ 32 categories \\\\\nRSSM stochastic dim & 32 \\\\\nRSSM deterministic dim & 512 \\\\\nMLP hidden size & 512 \\\\\nMLP layers & 2 \\\\\nActivation & SiLU \\\\\nNormalization & LayerNorm \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{2}{l}{\\textit{Training}} \\\\\nBatch size & 16 sequences $\\times$ 64 steps \\\\\nLearning rate & $3 \\times 10^{-4}$ (Adam, $\\epsilon{=}10^{-8}$) \\\\\nSequence length & 64 \\\\","numLines":120,"startLine":920,"totalLines":1174}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01L6qXBhkHgBbERiKZ2Wo5jn","type":"tool_result","content":"250\t\\label{sec:roc_analysis}\n251\t\n252\tThe original $n{=}17$ analysis (Tables~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b1}--\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full}) predates the SGS, RAVE, and TCN experiments. We extend the NVE diagnostic evaluation to $n{=}56$ configurations spanning all tested interventions. Figure~\\ref{fig:nve_roc} shows the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95\\% bootstrap confidence interval (10{,}000 resamples).\n253\t\n254\t\\begin{figure}[h]\n255\t\\centering\n256\t\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_roc_curve.pdf}\n257\t\\caption{NVE ROC curve ($n{=}56$ configurations, AUROC${=}0.990$, comprehensive validation). The preset $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$ operating point (star) achieves TPR${=}1.00$, FPR${=}0.09$, accuracy${=}53/56$, F1${=}0.941$. Three false positives arise from non-CIVO value overestimation: mitigation transient VE spike (008e\\_v3 subsample, $1.93\\times$) and frozen embedding transients (047, $1.71\\times$; 057, $1.88\\times$). Threshold calibrated and validated post-hoc; cross-architecture validation deferred.}\n258\t\\label{fig:nve_roc}\n259\t\\end{figure}\n260\t\n261\t\\begin{figure}[h]\n262\t\\centering\n263\t\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_threshold_prf.pdf}\n264\t\\caption{Precision, Recall, and F1 as a function of NVE threshold ($n{=}56$ configurations). Peak F1${=}0.941$ at $\\tau{=}1.5\\times$, where recall remains perfect ($1.00$) and precision${=}0.889$. The plateau of high F1 across $\\tau \\in [1.5, 1.7]$ indicates robustness to threshold selection.}\n265\t\\label{fig:nve_prf}\n266\t\\end{figure}\n267\t\n268\tWe label a configuration as CIVO-positive if and only if (i)~it uses a trained $\\dt$-embedding with multi-rate data exposure, and (ii)~NVE exceeds $1.5\\times$ with co-occurring entropy collapse. Configurations exhibiting high NVE through other mechanisms (gradient truncation side effects, value anchor pollution) are labeled non-CIVO.\n269\t\n270\tThe three false positives (FPR${=}0.18$) are mechanistically distinct from CIVO: (1)~RAVE anchor pollution (exp\\_028, the EMA anchor becomes inflated, producing overestimation through a different pathway); (2)~obs-decoder SGS-induced value distortion (exp\\_025 seed~2, blocking observation decoder gradients damages the RSSM latent space); (3)~IRD eval-driven collapse (exp\\_008e\\_v3 seed~2, actor entropy \\emph{increases} with evaluation collapse, mechanistically distinct from CIVO's entropy \\emph{decrease}). All three produce NVE $> 1.5\\times$ through non-CIVO mechanisms, indicating that the NVE diagnostic detects value overestimation broadly rather than CIVO specifically---a feature rather than a limitation for practitioners monitoring deployment health. The closest sub-threshold case (008f seed~4, NVE${=}1.41\\times$) lacks $\\dt$-conditioning entirely ($d{=}0$); its elevated NVE reflects transient value noise that self-corrects without the positive feedback loop characteristic of CIVO. The closest above-threshold positive (008d seed~3, NVE${=}1.53\\times$) exhibits the full CIVO causal chain: trained $\\dt$-embedding, entropy decrease, and evaluation collapse to 14\\% of baseline.\n271\t\n272\t\\paragraph{Comprehensive validation ($n{=}56$).}\n273\tExpanding the evaluation set to all classifiable experiments yields $n{=}56$ ($n_{\\text{pos}}{=}24$, $n_{\\text{neg}}{=}32$), spanning Walker Walk, Cheetah Run, and multiple intervention configurations (SGS, TCN, dual-critic, frozen embedding). At the $1.5\\times$ threshold: AUROC${=}0.990$, precision${=}0.889$, recall${=}1.000$, F1${=}0.941$, accuracy${=}53/56$. The three false positives are: exp\\_008e\\_v3\\_subsample ($1.93\\times$, mitigation config with transient VE spike), exp\\_047 ($1.71\\times$, frozen embedding transient), and exp\\_057 ($1.88\\times$, frozen embedding transient). All 24 CIVO-positive configurations are correctly detected (FN${=}0$), with CIVO-positive NVE ranging from $1.53\\times$ (008d seed~3, late-onset) to $70.64\\times$ (010b seed~0, Cheetah). The substantial increase in sample size from $n{=}32$ to $n{=}56$ strengthens confidence in the $1.5\\times$ threshold as a robust diagnostic boundary.\n274\t\n275\t\\subsection{NVE Normalization Robustness}\n276\t\\label{sec:nve_robustness}\n277\t\n278\tTo assess sensitivity to baseline seed choice, we extend the single-seed baseline (seed~1, eval 915.7 at 105K) to three additional seeds trained to 505K steps (Table~\\ref{tab:baseline_seeds}).\n279\t\n280\t\\begin{table}[h]\n281\t\\centering\n282\t\\caption{Walker Walk baseline seeds at 105K and 505K steps.}\n283\t\\label{tab:baseline_seeds}\n284\t\\footnotesize\n285\t\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n286\t\\toprule\n287\t\\textbf{Seed} & \\textbf{Eval@105K} & \\textbf{Eval@505K} & \\textbf{ve@65K} & \\textbf{ve@105K} \\\\\n288\t\\midrule\n289\ts1 & 915.7 & 970.4 & 0.563 & 0.656 \\\\\n290\ts2 & 443.5 & 945.7 & 0.898 & 0.742 \\\\\n291\ts3 & 869.0 & 947.7 & --- & 0.664 \\\\\n292\ts4 & 922.8 & 938.9 & --- & 0.624 \\\\\n293\t\\bottomrule\n294\t\\end{tabular}\n295\t\\end{table}\n296\t\n297\tSeed~2 exhibits slow convergence (eval 443.5 at 105K, recovering to 945.7 by 512K), confirming non-pathological slow convergence rather than seed failure. Its elevated $v/e$ ratio at 65K (0.898 vs.\\ 0.563 for seed~1) reflects the low evaluation denominator rather than pathological value overestimation. Using seed~2 as the sole normalization reference systematically deflates NVE values, causing two marginal CIVO-positive configurations (008d seed~3, peak NVE $1.53\\times$; 009b seed~2, peak NVE $1.62\\times$) to fall below the $1.5\\times$ threshold. Core CIVO cases (peak NVE $> 3\\times$) remain correctly classified under all baseline seeds.\n298\t\n299\tSingle-seed normalization (s1) yields AUROC $= 0.933$ and accuracy 7/8 (87.5\\%) on the Walker subset. Four-seed mean normalization yields AUROC $= 0.867$ and accuracy 6/8 (75.0\\%): the boundary case exp\\_009b flips from $\\nve = 1.62\\times$ (s1) to $1.23\\times$ (4-seed mean), because its peak occurs at 45K when the s1 $v/e$ ratio (0.331) is well below the 4-seed mean (0.436). All high-NVE configurations remain correctly classified (006: $4.84\\times \\to 4.52\\times$; 008d: $4.12\\times \\to 3.54\\times$). The $1.5\\times$ threshold thus correctly identifies all strong CIVO cases regardless of baseline choice; sensitivity is confined to configurations within 10\\% of the threshold."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a08170ba-d0ed-49ec-918a-a297ecfee54f","uuid":"2049b2b6-f437-4e56-8645-4e5958614b9a","timestamp":"2026-05-25T16:27:20.123Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_9/projects/event-gated-adaptive-horizon/docs/paper/sections/appendix.tex","content":"\\label{sec:roc_analysis}\n\nThe original $n{=}17$ analysis (Tables~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b1}--\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full}) predates the SGS, RAVE, and TCN experiments. We extend the NVE diagnostic evaluation to $n{=}56$ configurations spanning all tested interventions. Figure~\\ref{fig:nve_roc} shows the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95\\% bootstrap confidence interval (10{,}000 resamples).\n\n\\begin{figure}[h]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_roc_curve.pdf}\n\\caption{NVE ROC curve ($n{=}56$ configurations, AUROC${=}0.990$, comprehensive validation). The preset $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$ operating point (star) achieves TPR${=}1.00$, FPR${=}0.09$, accuracy${=}53/56$, F1${=}0.941$. Three false positives arise from non-CIVO value overestimation: mitigation transient VE spike (008e\\_v3 subsample, $1.93\\times$) and frozen embedding transients (047, $1.71\\times$; 057, $1.88\\times$). Threshold calibrated and validated post-hoc; cross-architecture validation deferred.}\n\\label{fig:nve_roc}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\begin{figure}[h]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_threshold_prf.pdf}\n\\caption{Precision, Recall, and F1 as a function of NVE threshold ($n{=}56$ configurations). Peak F1${=}0.941$ at $\\tau{=}1.5\\times$, where recall remains perfect ($1.00$) and precision${=}0.889$. The plateau of high F1 across $\\tau \\in [1.5, 1.7]$ indicates robustness to threshold selection.}\n\\label{fig:nve_prf}\n\\end{figure}\n\nWe label a configuration as CIVO-positive if and only if (i)~it uses a trained $\\dt$-embedding with multi-rate data exposure, and (ii)~NVE exceeds $1.5\\times$ with co-occurring entropy collapse. Configurations exhibiting high NVE through other mechanisms (gradient truncation side effects, value anchor pollution) are labeled non-CIVO.\n\nThe three false positives (FPR${=}0.18$) are mechanistically distinct from CIVO: (1)~RAVE anchor pollution (exp\\_028, the EMA anchor becomes inflated, producing overestimation through a different pathway); (2)~obs-decoder SGS-induced value distortion (exp\\_025 seed~2, blocking observation decoder gradients damages the RSSM latent space); (3)~IRD eval-driven collapse (exp\\_008e\\_v3 seed~2, actor entropy \\emph{increases} with evaluation collapse, mechanistically distinct from CIVO's entropy \\emph{decrease}). All three produce NVE $> 1.5\\times$ through non-CIVO mechanisms, indicating that the NVE diagnostic detects value overestimation broadly rather than CIVO specifically---a feature rather than a limitation for practitioners monitoring deployment health. The closest sub-threshold case (008f seed~4, NVE${=}1.41\\times$) lacks $\\dt$-conditioning entirely ($d{=}0$); its elevated NVE reflects transient value noise that self-corrects without the positive feedback loop characteristic of CIVO. The closest above-threshold positive (008d seed~3, NVE${=}1.53\\times$) exhibits the full CIVO causal chain: trained $\\dt$-embedding, entropy decrease, and evaluation collapse to 14\\% of baseline.\n\n\\paragraph{Comprehensive validation ($n{=}56$).}\nExpanding the evaluation set to all classifiable experiments yields $n{=}56$ ($n_{\\text{pos}}{=}24$, $n_{\\text{neg}}{=}32$), spanning Walker Walk, Cheetah Run, and multiple intervention configurations (SGS, TCN, dual-critic, frozen embedding). At the $1.5\\times$ threshold: AUROC${=}0.990$, precision${=}0.889$, recall${=}1.000$, F1${=}0.941$, accuracy${=}53/56$. The three false positives are: exp\\_008e\\_v3\\_subsample ($1.93\\times$, mitigation config with transient VE spike), exp\\_047 ($1.71\\times$, frozen embedding transient), and exp\\_057 ($1.88\\times$, frozen embedding transient). All 24 CIVO-positive configurations are correctly detected (FN${=}0$), with CIVO-positive NVE ranging from $1.53\\times$ (008d seed~3, late-onset) to $70.64\\times$ (010b seed~0, Cheetah). The substantial increase in sample size from $n{=}32$ to $n{=}56$ strengthens confidence in the $1.5\\times$ threshold as a robust diagnostic boundary.\n\n\\subsection{NVE Normalization Robustness}\n\\label{sec:nve_robustness}\n\nTo assess sensitivity to baseline seed choice, we extend the single-seed baseline (seed~1, eval 915.7 at 105K) to three additional seeds trained to 505K steps (Table~\\ref{tab:baseline_seeds}).\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Walker Walk baseline seeds at 105K and 505K steps.}\n\\label{tab:baseline_seeds}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Seed} & \\textbf{Eval@105K} & \\textbf{Eval@505K} & \\textbf{ve@65K} & \\textbf{ve@105K} \\\\\n\\midrule\ns1 & 915.7 & 970.4 & 0.563 & 0.656 \\\\\ns2 & 443.5 & 945.7 & 0.898 & 0.742 \\\\\ns3 & 869.0 & 947.7 & --- & 0.664 \\\\\ns4 & 922.8 & 938.9 & --- & 0.624 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nSeed~2 exhibits slow convergence (eval 443.5 at 105K, recovering to 945.7 by 512K), confirming non-pathological slow convergence rather than seed failure. Its elevated $v/e$ ratio at 65K (0.898 vs.\\ 0.563 for seed~1) reflects the low evaluation denominator rather than pathological value overestimation. Using seed~2 as the sole normalization reference systematically deflates NVE values, causing two marginal CIVO-positive configurations (008d seed~3, peak NVE $1.53\\times$; 009b seed~2, peak NVE $1.62\\times$) to fall below the $1.5\\times$ threshold. Core CIVO cases (peak NVE $> 3\\times$) remain correctly classified under all baseline seeds.\n\nSingle-seed normalization (s1) yields AUROC $= 0.933$ and accuracy 7/8 (87.5\\%) on the Walker subset. Four-seed mean normalization yields AUROC $= 0.867$ and accuracy 6/8 (75.0\\%): the boundary case exp\\_009b flips from $\\nve = 1.62\\times$ (s1) to $1.23\\times$ (4-seed mean), because its peak occurs at 45K when the s1 $v/e$ ratio (0.331) is well below the 4-seed mean (0.436). All high-NVE configurations remain correctly classified (006: $4.84\\times \\to 4.52\\times$; 008d: $4.12\\times \\to 3.54\\times$). The $1.5\\times$ threshold thus correctly identifies all strong CIVO cases regardless of baseline choice; sensitivity is confined to configurations within 10\\% of the threshold.","numLines":50,"startLine":250,"totalLines":1174}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01929F6cJJJFYzzWdwt7uio1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SaS4hB8HAT5gVVJcTm1NF4","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python3 -c \"\nfrom scipy.stats import beta as beta_dist\n\ndef cp_ci(k, n, alpha=0.05):\n    if k == 0:\n        lo = 0.0\n    else:\n        lo = beta_dist.ppf(alpha/2, k, n-k+1)\n    if k == n:\n        hi = 1.0\n    else:\n        hi = beta_dist.ppf(1-alpha/2, k+1, n-k)\n    return lo, hi\n\n# B2 full (n=16, n_pos=8, n_neg=8) - perfect separation\nprint('=== B2 full (n=16, n_pos=8, n_neg=8) ===')\nprint('AUROC = 1.000')\nthresholds = [\n    ('>=1.0', 8, 2, 0, 6),\n    ('>=1.2', 8, 0, 0, 8),\n    ('>=1.5', 8, 0, 0, 8),\n    ('>=1.7', 7, 0, 1, 8),\n    ('>=2.0', 7, 0, 1, 8),\n    ('>=3.9', 6, 0, 2, 8),\n]\nfor name, tp, fp, fn, tn in thresholds:\n    acc = (tp+tn)/16\n    prec = tp/(tp+fp) if (tp+fp) > 0 else 0\n    rec = tp/(tp+fn) if (tp+fn) > 0 else 0\n    f1 = 2*prec*rec/(prec+rec) if (prec+rec) > 0 else 0\n    lo, hi = cp_ci(tp+tn, 16)\n    print(f'{name}: TP={tp} FP={fp} FN={fn} TN={tn} Acc={acc*100:.1f}% [{lo*100:.1f}, {hi*100:.1f}] Prec={prec*100:.1f}% Rec={rec*100:.0f}% F1={f1*100:.1f}%')\n\"\n","description":"Compute n=16 B2 full sensitivity table"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":18678,"cache_read_input_tokens":48253,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":18678},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a08170ba-d0ed-49ec-918a-a297ecfee54f","uuid":"e1673870-72bb-4587-8871-9687c2e9bab7"}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Affs4wGaDuRkSA8oKkLnG5","type":"tool_result","content":"1070\tThis appendix provides the full algorithm specification and validation results for the online CIVO detector described in \\S\\ref{sec:detector}.\n1071\t\n1072\t\\subsection{Algorithm Specification}\n1073\t\n1074\t\n1075\tThe four conditions capture complementary signals: (1)~\\emph{Magnitude} ($r_t \\geq 0.49$) confirms that the value-to-evaluation ratio has reached a level indicative of overestimation; (2)~\\emph{Velocity} ($\\Delta r_t > 0.1$) rules out slow drift or plateau behavior; (3)~\\emph{Acceleration} ($\\Delta r_t > \\Delta r_{t-1}$, both $> 0.1$) filters oscillatory paths; (4)~\\emph{Evaluation decline} ($\\geq 2$ of 3 recent checkpoints decline) confirms that overestimation coincides with actual performance degradation. Despite using the hyperparameter combination that triggers collapse in all 10 tested multi-joint locomotion seeds (Walker/Cheetah), the single-joint Cartpole shows no CIVO, confirming the phenomenon requires multi-joint dynamics where temporal abstraction amplifies the reward fidelity gap.\n\n\\section{NVE Threshold Sensitivity Analysis}\n\\label{sec:appendix_sensitivity}\n\nWe report the full sensitivity analysis for the NVE diagnostic framework introduced in Section~\\ref{sec:results}. The main text reports Task~B2 (any CIVO detection, $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$). Here we additionally present Task~B1, which restricts the positive class to \\emph{sustained} CIVO, specifically experiments exhibiting persistent, accelerating value overestimation that progresses to performance collapse. Transient CIVO cases (e.g., exp~009b, which self-corrects after a brief excursion above the threshold) are classified as negative in B1.\n\n\\subsection{Per-Experiment NVE Values}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:nve_raw} lists the NVE values at 35K+ training steps for all eleven factorial experiments (including four 008e\\_v3 seeds and exp\\_059). Experiments are sorted by descending NVE. Experiment 008e\\_v3\\_s2 exhibits elevated NVE ($3.78\\times$) due to Imagination-Reality Divergence (IRD), a mechanistically distinct phenomenon from CIVO, and is classified as negative in both tasks. Experiment 008e\\_v3\\_s3 exhibits CIVO with NVE $4.02\\times$ despite $\\Delta t{=}1$ imagination.\n\n\\begin{table}[ht]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Per-experiment NVE values (35K+ steps) and ground truth labels. $+$ = positive (CIVO), $-$ = negative. IRD = Imagination-Reality Divergence; trans.\\ = transient CIVO with self-correction.}\n\\label{tab:nve_raw}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lrccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nExperiment & NVE & Mechanism & B1 & B2 \\\\\n\\midrule\n006          & 4.83 & sustained CIVO & $+$ & $+$ \\\\\n059          & 4.72 & self-correcting CIVO & $-$ & $+$ \\\\\n008d         & 4.12 & sustained CIVO & $+$ & $+$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s3 & 4.02 & CIVO           & $+$ & $+$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s2 & 3.78 & IRD (non-CIVO) & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n009b         & 1.62 & transient CIVO & $-$ & $+$ \\\\\n001          & 1.00 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s4 & 0.99 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008f         & 0.97 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008e\\_v3\\_s1 & 0.94 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n008a         & 0.93 & non-CIVO       & $-$ & $-$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Multi-Threshold Classification Performance}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b1} reports Task~B1 classification metrics across six NVE thresholds. Task~B1 achieves $\\text{AUROC} = 0.917$ because exp\\_059 (NVE${=}4.72\\times$, self-correcting CIVO, B1-negative) ranks above two sustained-CIVO positives ($4.12\\times$, $4.02\\times$), breaking the perfect rank separation that held before its inclusion. The optimal threshold lies in the interval $(3.78, 4.02]$; we report $\\geq 3.9\\times$ as a representative value (accuracy $10/11 = 90.9\\%$). Table~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2} provides the corresponding analysis for Task~B2 ($\\text{AUROC} = 0.967$, imperfect separation due to 008e\\_v3\\_s2).\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{\\textbf{Task~B1}: Sustained CIVO detection sensitivity analysis ($n_{\\text{pos}}=3$, $n_{\\text{neg}}=8$, $n=11$, $\\text{AUROC}=0.917$). All confidence intervals are two-sided Clopper-Pearson exact binomial ($\\alpha=0.05$). $^\\dagger$Optimal threshold in $(3.78, 4.02]$; exp\\_059 (NVE${=}4.72\\times$, B1-negative) is the sole false positive.}\n\\label{tab:sensitivity_b1}\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{5pt}\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nThreshold & TP & FP & FN & TN & Accuracy [95\\% CI] & Precision & Recall & F1 \\\\\n\\midrule\n$\\geq 1.0\\times$ & 3 & 4 & 0 & 4 & 63.6\\% \\; [30.8, 89.1] & 42.9\\% & 100\\% & 60.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.2\\times$ & 3 & 3 & 0 & 5 & 72.7\\% \\; [39.0, 94.0] & 50.0\\% & 100\\% & 66.7\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.5\\times$ & 3 & 3 & 0 & 5 & 72.7\\% \\; [39.0, 94.0] & 50.0\\% & 100\\% & 66.7\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 1.7\\times$ & 3 & 2 & 0 & 6 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 60.0\\% & 100\\% & 75.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 2.0\\times$ & 3 & 2 & 0 & 6 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 60.0\\% & 100\\% & 75.0\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 3.9\\times^\\dagger$ & 3 & 1 & 0 & 7 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 75.0\\% & 100\\% & 85.7\\% \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{\\textbf{Task~B2}: Any CIVO detection sensitivity analysis ($n_{\\text{pos}}=5$, $n_{\\text{neg}}=6$, $n=11$, $\\text{AUROC}=0.967$). The single false positive at $\\geq 1.5\\times$ is 008e\\_v3\\_s2 (IRD mechanism, not CIVO). The $1.5\\times$ threshold (highlighted) maximizes F1 while maintaining perfect recall.}\n\\label{tab:sensitivity_b2}\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{5pt}\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nThreshold & TP & FP & FN & TN & Accuracy [95\\% CI] & Precision & Recall & F1 \\\\\n\\midrule\n$\\geq 1.0\\times$ & 5 & 2 & 0 & 4 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 71.4\\% & 100\\% & 83.3\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.2\\times$ & 5 & 1 & 0 & 5 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 83.3\\% & 100\\% & 90.9\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 1.5\\times$ & 5 & 1 & 0 & 5 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 83.3\\% & 100\\% & 90.9\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.7\\times$ & 4 & 1 & 1 & 5 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 2.0\\times$ & 4 & 1 & 1 & 5 & 81.8\\% \\; [48.2, 97.7] & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% & 80.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 3.9\\times$ & 4 & 0 & 1 & 6 & 90.9\\% \\; [58.7, 99.8] & 100\\% & 80.0\\% & 88.9\\% \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\begin{table*}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{\\textbf{Task~B2 (full evaluation set)}: Any CIVO detection across two environments ($n_{\\text{pos}}=9$, $n_{\\text{neg}}=8$, $n=17$, $\\text{AUROC}=0.972$). Includes Walker Walk (15 configurations) and Cheetah Run (2 configurations).}\n\\label{tab:sensitivity_b2_full}\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{5pt}\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nThreshold & TP & FP & FN & TN & Accuracy [95\\% CI] & Precision & Recall & F1 \\\\\n\\midrule\n$\\geq 1.0\\times$ & 9 & 2 & 0 & 6 & 88.2\\% \\; [63.6, 98.5] & 81.8\\% & 100\\% & 90.0\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.2\\times$ & 9 & 1 & 0 & 7 & 94.1\\% \\; [71.3, 99.9] & 90.0\\% & 100\\% & 94.7\\% \\\\\n\\rowcolor{gray!15}\n$\\geq 1.5\\times$ & 9 & 1 & 0 & 7 & 94.1\\% \\; [71.3, 99.9] & 90.0\\% & 100\\% & 94.7\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 1.7\\times$ & 7 & 1 & 2 & 7 & 82.4\\% \\; [56.6, 96.2] & 87.5\\% & 77.8\\% & 82.4\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 2.0\\times$ & 7 & 1 & 2 & 7 & 82.4\\% \\; [56.6, 96.2] & 87.5\\% & 77.8\\% & 82.4\\% \\\\\n$\\geq 3.9\\times$ & 7 & 0 & 2 & 8 & 88.2\\% \\; [63.6, 98.5] & 100\\% & 77.8\\% & 87.5\\% \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table*}\n\n\\subsection{Threshold Recommendation}\n\nFor the main diagnostic (Task~B2), we recommend $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$ as the operating threshold for three reasons:\n\n\\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]\n\\item \\textbf{Maximum recall.} The $1.5\\times$ threshold achieves 100\\% recall, detecting all five CIVO cases including the transient case (009b, $\\nve = 1.62\\times$). Raising the threshold to $1.7\\times$ loses 009b, dropping recall to 80.0\\%.\n\\item \\textbf{Best F1.} At $1.5\\times$, F1 = 90.9\\%, the highest among all tested thresholds for B2. The single false positive (008e\\_v3\\_s2) is mechanistically identifiable as IRD rather than CIVO.\n\\item \\textbf{Sensitivity--specificity tradeoff.} Lower thresholds ($1.0\\times$) add false positives without gaining true positives. Higher thresholds ($\\geq 1.7\\times$) sacrifice recall without eliminating the 008e\\_v3\\_s2 false positive (which requires $\\tau > 3.78$).\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nFor Task~B1 (sustained CIVO only), the optimal threshold $\\nve \\geq 3.9\\times$ achieves $10/11$ accuracy ($90.9\\%$, 95\\% CI: [58.7\\%, 99.8\\%]); the sole false positive is exp\\_059 (NVE${=}4.72\\times$, self-correcting CIVO classified as B1-negative).\n\n\\subsection{Expanded ROC Analysis}\n\\label{sec:roc_analysis}\n\nThe original $n{=}17$ analysis (Tables~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b1}--\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full}) predates the SGS, RAVE, and TCN experiments. We extend the NVE diagnostic evaluation to $n{=}56$ configurations spanning all tested interventions. Figure~\\ref{fig:nve_roc} shows the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95\\% bootstrap confidence interval (10{,}000 resamples).\n\n\\begin{figure}[h]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_roc_curve.pdf}\n\\caption{NVE ROC curve ($n{=}56$ configurations, AUROC${=}0.990$, comprehensive validation). The preset $\\nve \\geq 1.5\\times$ operating point (star) achieves TPR${=}1.00$, FPR${=}0.09$, accuracy${=}53/56$, F1${=}0.941$. Three false positives arise from non-CIVO value overestimation: mitigation transient VE spike (008e\\_v3 subsample, $1.93\\times$) and frozen embedding transients (047, $1.71\\times$; 057, $1.88\\times$). Threshold calibrated and validated post-hoc; cross-architecture validation deferred.}\n\\label{fig:nve_roc}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\begin{figure}[h]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=0.7\\columnwidth]{../../artifacts/figures/nve_threshold_prf.pdf}\n\\caption{Precision, Recall, and F1 as a function of NVE threshold ($n{=}56$ configurations). Peak F1${=}0.941$ at $\\tau{=}1.5\\times$, where recall remains perfect ($1.00$) and precision${=}0.889$. The plateau of high F1 across $\\tau \\in [1.5, 1.7]$ indicates robustness to threshold selection.}\n\\label{fig:nve_prf}\n\\end{figure}\n\nWe label a configuration as CIVO-positive if and only if (i)~it uses a trained $\\dt$-embedding with multi-rate data exposure, and (ii)~NVE exceeds $1.5\\times$ with co-occurring entropy collapse. Configurations exhibiting high NVE through other mechanisms (gradient truncation side effects, value anchor pollution) are labeled non-CIVO.\n\nThe three false positives (FPR${=}0.18$) are mechanistically distinct from CIVO: (1)~RAVE anchor pollution (exp\\_028, the EMA anchor becomes inflated, producing overestimation through a different pathway); (2)~obs-decoder SGS-induced value distortion (exp\\_025 seed~2, blocking observation decoder gradients damages the RSSM latent space); (3)~IRD eval-driven collapse (exp\\_008e\\_v3 seed~2, actor entropy \\emph{increases} with evaluation collapse, mechanistically distinct from CIVO's entropy \\emph{decrease}). All three produce NVE $> 1.5\\times$ through non-CIVO mechanisms, indicating that the NVE diagnostic detects value overestimation broadly rather than CIVO specifically---a feature rather than a limitation for practitioners monitoring deployment health. The closest sub-threshold case (008f seed~4, NVE${=}1.41\\times$) lacks $\\dt$-conditioning entirely ($d{=}0$); its elevated NVE reflects transient value noise that self-corrects without the positive feedback loop characteristic of CIVO. The closest above-threshold positive (008d seed~3, NVE${=}1.53\\times$) exhibits the full CIVO causal chain: trained $\\dt$-embedding, entropy decrease, and evaluation collapse to 14\\% of baseline.\n\n\\paragraph{Comprehensive validation ($n{=}56$).}\nExpanding the evaluation set to all classifiable experiments yields $n{=}56$ ($n_{\\text{pos}}{=}24$, $n_{\\text{neg}}{=}32$), spanning Walker Walk, Cheetah Run, and multiple intervention configurations (SGS, TCN, dual-critic, frozen embedding). At the $1.5\\times$ threshold: AUROC${=}0.990$, precision${=}0.889$, recall${=}1.000$, F1${=}0.941$, accuracy${=}53/56$. The three false positives are: exp\\_008e\\_v3\\_subsample ($1.93\\times$, mitigation config with transient VE spike), exp\\_047 ($1.71\\times$, frozen embedding transient), and exp\\_057 ($1.88\\times$, frozen embedding transient). All 24 CIVO-positive configurations are correctly detected (FN${=}0$), with CIVO-positive NVE ranging from $1.53\\times$ (008d seed~3, late-onset) to $70.64\\times$ (010b seed~0, Cheetah). The substantial increase in sample size from $n{=}32$ to $n{=}56$ strengthens confidence in the $1.5\\times$ threshold as a robust diagnostic boundary.\n\n\\subsection{NVE Normalization Robustness}\n\\label{sec:nve_robustness}\n\nTo assess sensitivity to baseline seed choice, we extend the single-seed baseline (seed~1, eval 915.7 at 105K) to three additional seeds trained to 505K steps (Table~\\ref{tab:baseline_seeds}).\n\n\\begin{table}[h]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Walker Walk baseline seeds at 105K and 505K steps.}\n\\label{tab:baseline_seeds}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n\\textbf{Seed} & \\textbf{Eval@105K} & \\textbf{Eval@505K} & \\textbf{ve@65K} & \\textbf{ve@105K} \\\\\n\\midrule\ns1 & 915.7 & 970.4 & 0.563 & 0.656 \\\\\ns2 & 443.5 & 945.7 & 0.898 & 0.742 \\\\\ns3 & 869.0 & 947.7 & --- & 0.664 \\\\\ns4 & 922.8 & 938.9 & --- & 0.624 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nSeed~2 exhibits slow convergence (eval 443.5 at 105K, recovering to 945.7 by 512K), confirming non-pathological slow convergence rather than seed failure. Its elevated $v/e$ ratio at 65K (0.898 vs.\\ 0.563 for seed~1) reflects the low evaluation denominator rather than pathological value overestimation. Using seed~2 as the sole normalization reference systematically deflates NVE values, causing two marginal CIVO-positive configurations (008d seed~3, peak NVE $1.53\\times$; 009b seed~2, peak NVE $1.62\\times$) to fall below the $1.5\\times$ threshold. Core CIVO cases (peak NVE $> 3\\times$) remain correctly classified under all baseline seeds.\n\nSingle-seed normalization (s1) yields AUROC $= 0.933$ and accuracy 7/8 (87.5\\%) on the Walker subset. Four-seed mean normalization yields AUROC $= 0.867$ and accuracy 6/8 (75.0\\%): the boundary case exp\\_009b flips from $\\nve = 1.62\\times$ (s1) to $1.23\\times$ (4-seed mean), because its peak occurs at 45K when the s1 $v/e$ ratio (0.331) is well below the 4-seed mean (0.436). All high-NVE configurations remain correctly classified (006: $4.84\\times \\to 4.52\\times$; 008d: $4.12\\times \\to 3.54\\times$). The $1.5\\times$ threshold thus correctly identifies all strong CIVO cases regardless of baseline choice; sensitivity is confined to configurations within 10\\% of the threshold.\n\n\\paragraph{Normalization conventions.} Walker NVE is normalized against the single-seed baseline (seed~1, exp\\_001, 505K steps). Cheetah NVE is normalized against a 5-seed mean baseline (seeds~0--4, each run to ${\\sim}$210K steps). The differing seed counts reflect available baseline data; both provide sufficient coverage of the respective experimental windows (Walker: 210K analysis window; Cheetah: 105K analysis window).\n\n\\paragraph{Limitations.} The initial $n{=}11$ analysis had wide Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (e.g., 90.9\\% accuracy, 95\\% CI [58.7\\%, 99.8\\%]). The comprehensive evaluation ($n{=}56$, AUROC${=}0.990$, F1${=}0.941$; Figure~\\ref{fig:nve_roc}) substantially tightens these bounds. Table~\\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full} reports the $n{=}17$ two-environment core evaluation. Cross-architecture validation is deferred to future work.\n\n\\subsection{Leave-One-Environment-Out Cross-Validation}\n\\label{sec:nve_loeo}\n\nTo assess whether $\\theta{=}1.5\\times$ generalizes beyond the in-sample evaluation, we perform leave-one-environment-out (LOEO) cross-validation across Walker ($n{=}15$), Cheetah ($n{=}5$), and PickCube ($n{=}2$).
